edges.description: Altered POGZ function compromises the HP1-dependent repressive activity that POGZ exerts at pericentric heterochromatin.

Independently of its transcriptional-repressor role, POGZ is required for normal mitotic progression, so its loss reduces the number of dividing cortical progenitors. Curated as a separate arm from the transcriptional node because the reported intermediates are mitotic (kinetochore assembly and chromosome segregation) rather than transcriptional.

edges.description: Altered POGZ function perturbs its transcriptional-regulatory role in the nucleus.

The gastrointestinal phenotype is attributed to POGZ dysfunction itself rather than to the neurodevelopmental chain: the largest systematically surveyed cohort infers from the pattern of functional and anatomical involvement that POGZ participates in intestinal-tract development and motility. No intermediate mechanism has been established, so the specific feeding, swallowing, bowel and vomiting manifestations are not separately wired (see the multisystem knowledge-gap discussion).
Loss of the HP1-dependent repressive activity is the molecular basis for the transcriptional dysregulation - most conspicuously gene upregulation - seen when POGZ function is lost.
Perturbed transcriptional output in neural progenitors and developing neurons impairs cortical development.
Loss of POGZ's negative transcriptional regulation produces the largest gene upregulation in cerebellum, with a corresponding Purkinje cell defect.

POGZ regulatory targets overlap sleep-trait-associated genes, and pathway enrichment over that intersection implicates regulation of circadian rhythm, nominating transcriptional dysregulation of these targets as the route from POGZ loss to the sleep phenotype. The link is computational (in-silico enrichment) and the in-vivo intermediates are unverified; the same study found the sleep phenotype is not driven by obesity.
Early depletion of the cycling progenitor pool reduces the neurons available to build the cortex, which is the developmental lesion the downstream node represents.

edges.description: Reduced progenitor mitosis and premature differentiative exit limit the neuronal output of the developing brain, and the same Pogz-deficient mice have significantly lower brain weight. The mouse small-brain phenotype is explicitly related by the authors to human microcephaly, but the progenitor-to-head-size chain has not been traced step by step, so the edge carries unknown intermediates. Brain weight relative to body weight was higher in homozygous conditional knockouts, indicating a larger effect on body growth; reduced absolute brain weight therefore does not establish a brain-specific growth defect.

edges.description: Abnormal cortical development yields neurons with elevated intrinsic excitability.
Impaired cortical development underlies the cognitive impairment.

Impaired neuronal development is a proposed substrate for developmental abnormalities within the broader brain-morphology phenotype. This indirect summary edge does not establish that the cortical lesion causes every imaging finding: white matter changes, myelination abnormalities and atrophy may have different, unresolved intermediates.
Abnormal cortical development is the presumed substrate for the epilepsy; the intermediates are not established and no excitation/inhibition-imbalance claim is asserted.

The near-universal developmental delay is attributed to the same cortical developmental lesion that underlies the cognitive impairment; this is a summary edge of the same standing as the intellectual-disability edge.

Speech and language acquisition is the developmental domain most consistently and disproportionately affected; the cortical developmental lesion is the presumed substrate, and no domain-specific intermediate explaining the disproportion has been established.

Motor development is delayed as part of the global developmental impairment, with hypotonia contributing; cerebellar involvement (see the Purkinje cell node) may also contribute, but no human data apportion the motor delay between cortical and cerebellar substrates.

Hypotonia is part of the neurological examination profile of this central nervous system developmental disorder and is attributed to the brain developmental lesion; no peripheral or neuromuscular cause has been implicated, and no specific intermediates are established.
Impaired cortical network development is the proposed cellular substrate for the behavioural phenotype beyond autism; the intermediates are not established.

The cohort literature attributes gait abnormalities to neurological substrates - spasticity, hypotonia or discoordination - rather than a primary musculoskeletal cause, tying this manifestation to the central nervous system lesion.
The same conditional-knockout model that shows the cerebellar defect also reproduces microcephaly and growth impairment.
Elevated excitability underlies the social deficits in the mouse model, the behavioural correlate of the human autistic phenotype.
Models impaired neuronal differentiation and migration in human patient-derived neural cells.

It is curated as a parallel arm to the cortical node rather than subsumed into it, because the two models implicate different circuits and, notably, report opposite social phenotypes.

nodes.description: POGZ localises to pericentric heterochromatin in the same distribution as HP1-alpha and represses transcription in a dual-luciferase reporter assay. That repression is HP1-dependent: an H840A substitution in the HP1-binding zinc-finger-like (HPZ) domain, which abolishes the POGZ-HP1-alpha interaction, also abolishes repression. The HP1-binding step is therefore the molecular mechanism by which POGZ acts as a negative regulator of transcription, and is the specific activity lost in White-Sutton syndrome. The evidence is in vitro (HEK293 reporter assay, N2A immunofluorescence), so this node is curated at provisional confidence.

nodes.description: Heterozygous nonsense, frameshift and splice variants, and a minority of missense variants, in POGZ reduce or alter the function of a multidomain nuclear protein. The genotype-phenotype relationship is not a simple dosage gradient: missense variants are associated with milder phenotypes, while truncating variants predicted to ESCAPE nonsense-mediated decay produce the most severe phenotypes, and within that group variants in the proline-rich region are the most severe of all. The authors infer that a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect from a stable truncated protein may contribute to the severe end of the spectrum, but this allelic mechanism has not been demonstrated experimentally.

nodes.description: In the embryonic (E15.5) cerebral cortex of Pogz-deficient mice the number of pHH3-positive mitotic cells is significantly reduced and the Tbr2-positive intermediate-progenitor layer is correspondingly expanded, while the Pax6-positive apical-progenitor layer is unchanged. The authors interpret this as accelerated exit from the cell cycle - a shift from symmetric proliferative to asymmetric differentiative division - which depletes the progenitor pool available to generate cortical neurons. The finding is mouse-only, so this node is curated at provisional confidence.
